fatal_errors: The proposed TiVNbTa-to-TiVNbTaMo modification does not reconstruct the target comparison between CrFeTaVW and Ta-substituted CrFeTiVW.
It omits the target mechanical-alloying, spark-plasma-sintering, and hybrid MD/Monte Carlo atom-swap interventions.

The predicted strengthening mechanism is unrelated to the target mechanisms of chemical rearrangement, W association, Fe2Ta Laves-phase formation, multielement phonon scattering, and temperature-dependent lattice expansion.
No thermal-diffusivity prediction or measurement is provided, despite heat transfer being central to the target and Mo potentially changing thermal transport.
The claimed 20–30% high-temperature strength increase and retained ductility have no cited or composition-specific supporting evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad idea of improving an HEA interlayer and gives a controlled baseline-versus-modified mechanical test, but it concerns the wrong alloy system, intervention, observables, and mechanism. The target studied Ta-to-Ti substitution in CrFeTaVW/CrFeTiVW using MD versus hybrid MD/MC, mechanical alloying, SPS, phase and segregation characterization, and thermal diffusivity from 300–1000 K. The generated experiment could test its own strength claim, although XRD/TEM alone would not directly establish increased dislocation resistance or lattice-distortion strengthening. Its boundary statement also overextends results near 1273 K to W–CuCrZr service without testing thermal diffusivity, thermal cycling, interfacial compatibility, or the narrower CuCrZr operating window. Thus it is neither a reconstruction nor a sufficiently evidenced alternative.
